title: Research: shared target donors save 3,288 R420 XORs (no new kappa)
head: 6e7a5d271a123886dc7b54ca3180d0b9f9beda5a
body:
This **finite bit-circuit construction / research contribution** saves **3,288 binary XOR additions** in eumemic's accepted #543 R420 word: **26,916 → 23,628** complete native ADDs. A forest of shared target donors reduces frame-zero compensation D from **19,922 → 16,634**, including all **100 preparation and 100 restoration additions**. **No new κ is claimed.**

Sixteen nominated donors serve 100 receivers, with donor and receiver sets disjoint. Helpers remain untouched throughout D. The complete MOVE/COPY/ERASE subsequence, 420 helpers, nine copies, per-register frame paths and paid rank mass 5,112 are unchanged. The inverse positive-prefix bound increases to 3,798,646; the exact native payload bound remains within 104 bits (bit length 102).

Concurrent #713 (Scott Woolsey Biggart) and #716 (Sagar Thakrar) report 3,150 savings using disjoint target pairs. This extends the circuit class to **shared donors**, yielding 138 additional savings on the same baseline. Their target-basis work and Dugongue's #476/#478 identity are credited; no concurrent code or recipe is imported, and no priority for reversible target factoring is claimed. #686/#694's helper-basis constructions are also credited; #694 saves more overall and is not superseded. No combined saving is claimed.

The original syntactic H2 rule and literal K extractor deliberately reject this word. The package proves and checks the sufficient semantic replacement: D stays at frame zero and implements exactly `(x,s,y) -> (x,s,y+Ks)` for arbitrary initial targets and helpers. All other inherited interface diagnostics pass. No predecessor checker is patched.

Reproduce with Python 3.9+ and the standard library:

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-target-star/verify.py
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_R420_TARGET_STAR receivers=100 D=19922->16634 native_ADDs=26916->23628 saved=3288 columns=660 rank_mass=5112
```

The README also gives an optional fresh C++17/Boost replay command, checked against committed normalized `NATIVE.json` receipts.

Validation completed locally on macOS arm64, Python 3.9.6, Apple Clang 21.0.0 and authenticated Boost 1.85.0 headers:

- All 672 closed frames and 660 symbolic input columns, the exact D operator, and independent set-valued forward/inverse execution of the actual exported records.
- Both words replayed at 5/9/11 stages on 900/1,380/1,620 physical columns in Python and in freshly compiled unchanged C++ checkers. All 48 changed-stream bridge omissions are replayed literally in Python; the native built-in controls pass for both words.
- Nine construction/accounting controls, including a missing preparation invisible to zero-target tests, an already-modified receiver incorrectly used as donor, and an F2-neutral pair charged two ADDs. The C++ checkers reject a missing exported preparation at all three stage counts.
- Optimized/isolated Python, exact native-receipt comparison, minimal relocated reproduction, changed-source/certificate rejection, canonical output equality under gzip recompression, `make selected-record-check`, and staged whitespace checks pass.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Reviewed PR543 source: `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`. Selected #626 remains κ = `0.001635527380375392`, complex-limited. Exact SHA-256/Git-blob source pins, certificates, proof, validation, overlap metadata and local claim are included.

Assignment seed **0**, drawn once from OS randomness, selects the bit track and first donor target 0. The one evidence-driven extension after #713/#716 arrived permits shared donors. All **14,280** oriented pair costs and **1,680** candidate donor sets were evaluated, stopping at the preset **16-donor limit**. The best receiver assignment for a fixed donor set is proved; the greedy donor set has **no optimality claim**. No pinned coordination issue existed. Final overlap was refreshed through #735; main was unchanged. New #731 independently audits the baseline compensation rank, and #733 reports 8,368 savings by combining helper and target bases. They are credited and not imported. #733 changes helper values during D; this result retains the immutable-helper restriction and permits shared target donors. No overall saving record is claimed.

Only `research/r420-target-star/` is added. Acceptance of the semantic D interface, hosted-parent/whole-owner reconstruction, global prefix bounds, full finite invoices and changed-word outer assembly remain integration work. All inherited all-size/common-label/mutable-basis/hosting/residual/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain. Full repository `make verify`, selected cold reconstruction, remote Linux CI and Lean were not run or claimed. This is not a full multiplication proof or measured runtime improvement. `upstream/` and the selected frontier are unchanged.

Prepared for **@ellipsi2 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** in construction, reasoning, implementation, verification and packaging, under Apache-2.0. Original notices and cumulative predecessor attribution are retained. No independent human review is claimed.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
